summary: Sometimes, putting the rules of this law into practice causes a problem or a roadblock. To fix this, the Central Government can issue an official order to remove the difficulty. However, the government can only do this within a limited time and must show the order to Parliament.
points: The Central Government can make provisions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act.
Such provisions must be made by an order published in the Official Gazette.
The new provisions must not go against any part of this Act and must be necessary or expedient.
No such order can be made after five years from the date section 1 of the Act starts.
Every order made under this section must be laid before each House of Parliament as soon as possible after it is made.
example: When Starburst Electronics Private Limited tried to follow a new rule under the Companies Act, 2013, a confusing overlap in the paperwork caused a sudden roadblock for their business registration. Because many other companies faced the exact same issue, the Central Government used its special powers to issue an official order in the Gazette to clear up the confusion. This fixed the problem without breaking any existing laws. Afterward, the government placed a copy of that order before both Houses of Parliament to keep everyone informed.

terms.meaning: An official government publication used to give public notice of legal rules and orders.
The legislative chambers of the country, namely Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

watch: Remember that the government cannot use this power forever, as it stops working five years after section 1 commences.
